text: What should the collect-and-hold mode be called?
context: "Gem Grab" is another game's mode name, so this mode needs an original name before its key, `GameMode` variant, game-type IDs, and HUD text are fixed. The rules (collect, carry, hold a threshold) don't change. Hot Zone and Heist share the same issue, but they already ship, so renaming them would be a separate ticket if you want one.

suggestions.detail: Resource: shards. A short and readable name that fits the arcade tone, and it sits well next to "Wipeout".
Resource: power cores. Leans towards the facility and industrial map themes.
Resource: sparks. Leans towards the toon/HDR glow look, so shards and sparks read well with bloom.

text: Should a carrier stay hidden in concealment (tall grass)?
context: `docs/04-maps-and-game-modes.md` lists "visibility pressure" as part of this mode family, but the spec never decided it. It changes the server interest/concealment rules (`docs/17-concealment.md`) and how bots hunt carriers.

suggestions.text: Carriers at or above a threshold are revealed
suggestions.detail: A fighter carrying, say, 3 or more is visible through concealment to the enemy team. Big carriers can't hide in the grass and must be protected in the open. Small carriers can still sneak.
Any carrier is visible. This is the simplest to read, but it makes concealment nearly irrelevant to the mode.
Carriers hide like anyone else. This is the cheapest option, but a winning team can stall in the grass during the countdown.

text: What happens to the hold countdown when the leading team drops below the target?
context: The spec left this as "cancels or resets according to the authored rule".

suggestions.detail: The countdown stops and starts again from the full duration the next time the team reaches the target. Comebacks stay meaningful and the rule is easy to read.
The countdown keeps its remaining time and resumes when the target is reached again. This favours the leader and produces fewer dramatic swings.
